groups.title: Content of Feedback
groups.synthesis: Environmental impact is communicated through different types of indicators, making options comparable. These include outcome-oriented indicators (environmental metrics) and process-oriented indicators (behavioral metrics).
groups.practices: Carbon emissions, energy consumption, water usage, food impact, behavioral counts (e.g., number of green trips, check-in days).

groups.title: Format & Modality
groups.synthesis: Different representation formats influence readability, intuitiveness, and emotional engagement, shaping how users perceive and compare options.
groups.practices: Percentages, numerical values (e.g., kg CO₂), textual explanations, benchmark references (e.g., average users), icons such as a green leaf, charts (e.g., line and bar), grading labels (e.g., A–E), gamified rewards (e.g., points, badges).

groups.title: Reminders
groups.synthesis: The timing and frequency of feedback influence its role, including decision support, post-hoc reflection, and long-term reinforcement.
groups.practices: Real-time energy alerts, booking-time recommendations such as low-carbon routes, post-action summaries (e.g., weekly reports), different push frequencies (e.g., daily or periodic).

groups.title: Motivation & Choice
groups.synthesis: Comparative eco-feedback mainly presents information, but it also has the potential to intervene in decision-making by guiding attention, simplifying choices, and structuring available options.
groups.practices: Occasional highlighting of low-carbon options or simple recommendations. Systematic strategies such as default options, option ordering, filtering mechanisms, and commitment devices are largely absent across tools.

groups.title: Green Community & Identity
groups.synthesis: Eco-feedback reinforces environmental identity and a sense of belonging, linking behavior to social recognition.
groups.practices: Eco badges such as Eco Champion, social sharing, likes, peer comparison (e.g., using less energy than others), identity-related cues.

groups.title: Collective Action & Campaigns
groups.synthesis: Individual behavior is embedded within collective outcomes, encouraging participation, collaboration, and shared goals.
groups.practices: Community-level emission reduction data (e.g., total CO₂ reduction), group challenges, collaborative activities.

groups.title: Green Education & Norm Shaping
groups.synthesis: By conveying social norms and knowledge, eco-feedback supports understanding and adoption of sustainable behavior.
groups.practices: Statements such as “most people recycle,” explanations of environmental impact, descriptions of why behaviors matter.
